questions.question: When taking the first exit on the left at a roundabout, which lane do you choose?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 says to approach in the left-hand lane for the first exit.

questions.question: What MUST you do when a school crossing patrol holds up a red and yellow Stop sign?
options: Stop and wait until they lower the sign
Only stop if children are in your lane
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 210 says you MUST stop when signalled by a school crossing patrol.

questions.question: When may you pass a steady amber traffic light?
options: Whenever you are in a hurry
Only if you have crossed the line or cannot stop safely
questions.explain: Rule 175: you may only go on amber if stopping suddenly could cause a crash.

questions.question: What MUST you do once a pedestrian has moved onto a zebra crossing?
questions.explain: Rule 195 states you MUST give way when a pedestrian has moved onto a crossing.

questions.question: Where can you check which lane leads to your exit before reaching a busy roundabout?
options: Advance signs and painted arrows on the road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 tells drivers to read signs and road markings early.

questions.question: What do flashing amber lights on a school warning sign mean?
options: Children are crossing or nearby, so slow down
questions.explain: Rule 208: flashing amber lights show that a school crossing or children are active ahead.

questions.question: What colour comes immediately after a single steady amber light?
questions.explain: Rule 175: in the UK sequence, green goes to amber, then to red.

questions.question: What flashing lights mark a UK zebra crossing?
options: Amber Belisha beacons on black-and-white poles
questions.explain: Rule 195: flashing amber Belisha beacons warn drivers of a zebra crossing ahead.

questions.question: When taking the third exit to the right at a two-lane roundabout, which lane is usual?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses the right-hand lane for exits to the right unless signed otherwise.

questions.question: What do yellow 'SCHOOL KEEP CLEAR' zig-zag lines outside a school mean?
options: Do not wait, stop, or park there
questions.explain: Rule 238: keep school entrance zig-zags clear so children and drivers can see each other.

questions.question: Where should you stop for someone on a zebra crossing?
questions.explain: Rule 195: stop behind the dashed line so pedestrians have the full width of the crossing.

questions.question: You see a ball bounce into the road near a school. What should you do?
options: Slow down and be ready to stop in case a child runs after it
questions.explain: Rule 208: a child may follow a ball into the road without looking.

questions.question: A car in the lane beside you stops at a zebra crossing. What should you do?
options: Stop too, as a pedestrian may be crossing out of sight
questions.explain: Rule 191: never overtake a vehicle stopped at a crossing; someone may be hidden behind it.

questions.question: What do the white zig-zag lines beside a pedestrian crossing mean?
options: You must not park or overtake there
You may park for five minutes
You must speed up past the crossing
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids parking and overtaking within crossing zig-zag lines.

questions.question: When may you enter a yellow criss-cross box junction to go straight ahead?
options: Whenever the traffic lights are green
Only when your exit road is clear
When the car ahead is still moving slowly
At any time if you signal
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 states you must not enter a box junction unless your exit is clear.

questions.question: At speeds up to 30 mph, how much side space should you leave when overtaking a cyclist?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 says to leave at least 1.5 metres when overtaking cyclists up to 30 mph.

questions.question: What minimum gap should you leave behind the car in front on a dry road?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 sets at least a two-second gap in dry conditions.

questions.question: When should you give a signal before turning or changing lanes?
options: In good time before you make the move
Only when another car is behind you
Only at night or in rain
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 tells you to give clear signals in good time.

questions.question: What is the national speed limit for a car in a built-up area with street lights, unless signed otherwise?
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 sets 30 mph as the standard built-up area limit for cars.

questions.question: What do red and amber lights showing together mean?
options: Also means stop; do not pass until green shows
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 175 says RED AND AMBER also means stop; you must wait for green.

questions.question: Why must you NEVER drive anti-clockwise around a roundabout?
options: You would drive head-on into oncoming circulating traffic
It wears out the left tyres
It is allowed only for emergency vans
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 prevents head-on collisions by keeping all traffic clockwise.

questions.question: At a mini-roundabout, does the same give-way-to-the-right rule apply?
options: Yes, give way to traffic from your right just like a full roundabout
Traffic from the left goes first
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and 188 apply the same give-way-to-the-right rule at mini-roundabouts.

questions.question: Why do many drivers drift out of lane on roundabouts?
options: Looking only at the kerb instead of planning their path around the curve
Holding the steering wheel with both hands
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 advises looking ahead along your lane path to hold a clean line.

questions.question: If the roundabout is completely clear to your right, must you still stop?
options: No, keep moving smoothly if it is safe and clear
Yes, stop for three seconds every time
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 requires giving way, not stopping unnecessarily when the way is clear.

questions.question: When turning right at a small mini-roundabout, what mistake do learners sometimes make?
options: Cutting the corner on the wrong side of the white circle
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 185 and Rule 188 warn drivers not to cut across the wrong side of the central marking.

questions.question: If you want to change lanes while circulating on a roundabout, what must you do first?
options: Check mirrors and blind spot, signal, and wait for a clear gap
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 and Rule 133 require full checks before changing lanes.

questions.question: What tells you a 20 mph zone has ended?
options: A sign showing the new limit, such as 30
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 124 requires following the signed limit until a new limit sign appears.

questions.question: When must you stop completely behind a solid white line with a red octagonal STOP sign?
options: Every time, even if the road looks clear
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 171 and Rule 172 require a full stop at a STOP sign and line.

questions.question: Does Rule H2 apply when you turn out of a side road as well as when you turn into one?
options: Yes, both turning into and out of a road
questions.explain: Rule H2 covers pedestrians crossing or waiting to cross a road you are turning into or out of.

questions.question: Before moving close to the left kerb for a left turn, what should you check?
options: Your nearside mirror and blind spot for cyclists
questions.explain: Rule 182 warns to watch out for cyclists coming up on your left.

questions.question: Why should you look over your shoulder before moving into another lane?
options: Because mirrors do not show every blind spot
To wave thank you to cars behind
To see if your brake lights work
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 warns that mirrors cannot cover every blind spot beside your car.

questions.question: Which lane should you use on a multi-lane dual carriageway when you are not overtaking?
questions.explain: Rule 160: highway Code Rule 264 says keep in the left lane unless overtaking.

questions.question: Why should you avoid signalling left too early when going straight ahead?
options: Waiting drivers may think you are taking the first exit and pull out
It is illegal on motorways only
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 avoids early left signals so waiting traffic is not misled.

questions.question: Who benefits most from a clear left exit signal on a roundabout?
options: Drivers waiting at the next entrance to join the roundabout
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 uses exit signals to show waiting drivers you are leaving.

questions.question: You have already crossed the first white line when the light turns amber and you cannot stop safely there. What must you do?
options: Stop at the second white line
questions.explain: Rule 178 says if you cannot stop safely at the first line, stop at the second white line.

questions.question: The light is red, and there is a green left filter arrow lit. What may you do?
options: Turn left if safe, watching for pedestrians
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 177 allows you to move only in the direction of the green filter arrow.

questions.question: Why are STOP signs placed at certain junctions instead of Give Way signs?
options: Because the view of the main road is poor
questions.explain: Rule 171: sTOP signs are used where sightlines are restricted so drivers must stop and look carefully.

questions.question: What if a pedestrian is waiting to cross the side road you are turning into?
options: Give way and let them cross safely
Wave them back and turn fast
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 170 and Rule 172 require giving way to pedestrians crossing side roads.

questions.question: Before stopping to let a pedestrian cross a side road you are turning into, what should you check?
options: Your mirrors so you brake safely
questions.explain: Rule H2: check your mirrors early so you can slow down smoothly without surprising traffic behind.

questions.question: Should you slow down before you start steering into a tight left turn?
options: Yes, brake in a straight line before turning
questions.explain: Rule 182 advises adjusting your speed smoothly before reaching the corner.

questions.question: May you overtake a parked car that broke down on the zig-zags? Only if safe?
options: Wait if unsure, and pass slowly only if it is clearly stationary and broken down, watching for pedestrians
Never pass a broken-down car even after checking
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 forbids overtaking moving or stopped-for-crossing lead vehicles; pass broken-down obstructions only with extreme care.

questions.question: At a box junction, you follow a tall van and cannot see if space is clear beyond the box. What should you do?
options: Hold back before the box until you can see your exit is clear
Follow the van closely into the box
Overtake the van inside the box
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 means never entering blindly when a tall vehicle hides the exit.

questions.question: Approaching a blind hill crest behind a slow cyclist, what should you do?
options: Wait behind until you can see the oncoming road is clear
Overtake on the blind crest anyway
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 163 and Rule 166 forbid overtaking where you cannot see far enough ahead.

questions.question: If a driver behind is tailgating you, how should you respond?
options: Ease off slightly to leave more space in front so you can brake gently
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 126 advises increasing your front gap so neither car has to brake sharply.

questions.question: Two side roads are close together on your left and you want the second one. When should you signal?
options: As you pass the first side road
100 metres before the first side road
After turning into the second road
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 103 warns not to signal before an earlier turning you are not taking.

questions.question: In slow queuing traffic, when should you change lanes?
options: Whenever a tiny gap opens for a moment
Only when it is safe and you will not block others
As fast as possible before the queue stops
Without signalling so others do not speed up
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 133 advises not weaving between lanes or cutting across other drivers.

questions.question: Why is a right signal on approach helpful to drivers waiting at the left-hand entrance?
options: It warns them you are staying on the roundabout past their exit
It tells them to pull out in front of you
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 helps waiting drivers judge whether you will cross their path.

questions.question: You are in the right-hand lane of a two-lane roundabout and want to exit. What must you check before signalling left and moving out?
options: Your left mirror and blind spot for vehicles on your left
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 186 requires checking left before moving across to exit.

questions.question: Why are zig-zag lines painted on BOTH the approach and exit sides of a crossing?
options: To keep views clear in both directions and stop overtaking or parking near the stripes
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 191 keeps both sides of the crossing clear for pedestrians and drivers.

questions.question: Which turning direction has the special exception to wait inside a yellow box junction?
options: Turning right (when only oncoming traffic stops you)
questions.explain: Highway Code Rule 174 grants the exception only for right turns blocked by oncoming traffic.
